solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One showing off pustule, festering inside

indicators.note: inside says one word sits within the other, splitting it apart

blocks.note: a boil is a pustule on the skin

explanation.surface: A show-off has an infected spot that is getting worse.
explanation.walkthrough: Bobadil is the swaggering braggart soldier in Ben Jonson's play Every Man in His Humour, whose name became a byword.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobadil, from Jonson's play, became a byword for a boastful braggart, someone forever showing off.

clue.text: Middle of bra in its place gave way suddenly

indicators.note: middle of asks for only the central letter of the following word
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the central letter of the word bra
the bust is where a bra is worn

explanation.surface: A bra's centre gave way unexpectedly while being worn.
explanation.definitionFit: To burst is to break open or give way suddenly under pressure.

clue.text: Special treatment year after senior citizen admits commotion

indicators.note: admits means lets something inside, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: a pother is a fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: A pensioner caused a fuss and got special treatment a year later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Year after' puts the year's letter at the end. Opotherapy is treatment with extracts of animal organs.
explanation.definitionFit: Opotherapy is a specialised medical treatment using glandular extracts, so it is a particular kind of therapy.

clue.text: Something to mix with coke making graduate woolly

blocks.note: a cardi, short for cardigan, is a woolly jumper

explanation.surface: A mixer for cola that turns a graduate fuzzy-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: A woolly here is a knitted garment; a cardi is a cardigan.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacardi is a brand of rum, commonly drunk mixed with Coca-Cola.

clue.text: Expert one receiving turn in hallowed dome

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so a piece is lodged within another

blocks.note: a dab, or dab hand, is an expert
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: An expert takes a turn inside a holy dome.
explanation.walkthrough: A dab hand is an expert, shortened to dab. A dagoba is a Buddhist stupa.
explanation.definitionFit: A dagoba is a dome-shaped Buddhist shrine holding relics, so a sacred domed structure.

clue.text: Tortuous road climb, typical of N. Italian region

indicators.note: tortuous means full of twists, so the letters are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: A winding mountain road is characteristic of northern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lombardic means of Lombardy, the region of northern Italy around Milan.

clue.text: Round check collars, bent in the old style

indicators.note: to collar is to grab round the neck, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: to curb is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: A round check grabs someone who is crooked, in an old-fashioned way.
explanation.walkthrough: Blocks are listed outer then inner: CURB holds O after its first letter. Courb is an old (Shakespearean) verb and adjective meaning bend or bent.
explanation.definitionFit: Courb is an archaic form meaning curved or bent, as 'in the old style' signals.

clue.text: Stack of bricks left in permanent depot

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a camp is a settled base, as of an army

explanation.surface: A pile of bricks has been abandoned at a permanent storage site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as abandoned, but it is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamp is a heap of bricks stacked for firing, a sense found in brickmaking.

clue.text: Tricky bout circumvented by neat defeat in ring

indicators.note: tricky suggests something not straightforward, so its letters are rearranged
circumvented by means surrounded by, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox

explanation.surface: A tricky boxing bout is lost neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: Neat looks like an adjective but is the old noun for cattle. Outbox means to beat an opponent at boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: To outbox someone is to defeat them in a boxing ring by superior skill.

clue.text: Awful old racket from flautists

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the following word

explanation.surface: Flute players make a terrible din.
explanation.walkthrough: Utis is a Shakespearean word for a noisy riot or din.
explanation.definitionFit: Utis is an archaic word for a confused uproar or din, a terrible noise.

clue.text: Wild ox – number, specific one, in total caught

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a bag is the total game caught by a hunter

explanation.surface: A hunter counts the wild oxen killed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Total caught' reads as one phrase: a hunter's bag. A banteng is a wild ox of Southeast Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The banteng is a species of wild cattle found in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: One given a clout roughly – what a surprise! – for ungrammatical constructions

indicators.note: roughly means not precisely, so the letters come out in rough order

blocks.note: ha is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone gets roughly cuffed, surprisingly, for bad grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: An anacoluthon (plural anacolutha) is a sentence that switches construction midway.
explanation.definitionFit: Anacolutha are sentences that break off from their grammatical pattern, so ungrammatical constructions.

clue.text: Seabird revealing sample of petrochemicals inside

indicators.note: a sample is a small piece taken from within, so a run of letters is lifted from the word

explanation.surface: A seabird is found contaminated with petrochemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: Roch, also rotch, is the little auk.
explanation.definitionFit: The roch or rotch is a dialect name for the little auk, a small Arctic seabird.

clue.text: I'll replace Rex in an old lady's embrace, making love rarely

indicators.note: will replace says one letter is to take another's place

blocks.note: an and a are the same article
a matron is a staid older woman
R is short for rex, king
surface padding: says the king's letter is held within the old lady

explanation.surface: A man boasts he will take over a king's place in an older woman's arms.
explanation.walkthrough: The R held within A MATRON gives way to I. Amation is a rare word for loving.
explanation.definitionFit: Amation, from Latin amare, is a rare word for the act of loving or lovemaking.

clue.text: Tackling the drink, love ace noggin, getting sloshed

indicators.note: sloshed means drunk, and a drunk's letters stagger out of order

blocks.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A drinker downs an excellent noggin and gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for the sea; 'tackling' it means going to sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink is slang for the sea, and an oceangoing vessel takes on the open sea.

clue.text: Always welcomed, tons moved to extend visit (6, two words)

indicators.note: welcomed means taken in, so one piece is held within another
moved means shifted about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: ay, or aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A guest who is always welcome, with tons to do, stays longer.
explanation.walkthrough: Ay (or aye) means 'always', as in 'for ay'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay on is to remain longer than planned, so to prolong a visit.

clue.text: Dispatch written up in jottings for celebrity

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is set bottom to top
in places one piece inside the other

explanation.surface: A message noted down in jottings is reckoned to be fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Notedness is the state of being well known, which is what celebrity means.

clue.text: Pulse requiring short time, put in to boil initially

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so a piece is lodged within another
initially asks for only the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: hr is the short form of hour

explanation.surface: A heartbeat quickens when something is briefly put on to boil.
explanation.walkthrough: HR goes inside TO, then B follows. 'Short time' looks like a vague brief moment, but it is an abbreviated hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong regular beat, as of the heart, so a pulse.

clue.text: Work over? Jock's hardly open about that as culmination

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: agee is Scots for slightly open, ajar
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's door, barely ajar, marks the end of his work.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a nickname for a Scot, so the word wanted is Scots. 'That' points back to the reversed work.
explanation.definitionFit: The apogee is the highest point of an orbit, hence the peak or climax of anything.

clue.text: Die wretchedly in bed? She interceded

definitions.note: a clause standing for a noun: a woman who intercedes

indicators.note: wretchedly suggests a sorry, mangled state, so the letters are jumbled
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a matrix is the bed of rock in which something is embedded

explanation.surface: A woman pleaded on behalf of someone dying miserably in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' suggests a sickbed, but it is the geological sense, a matrix of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A mediatrix is a female mediator, a woman who intercedes between parties.

clue.text: Mottled or streaky lamb half reared, wild

indicators.note: half says only half of the word is kept, the rest dropped
wild means out of control, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: A lamb, half raised, runs wild with a streaky coat.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half of reared, RED, joins LAMB before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Marbled describes a surface veined or streaked like marble, as is fatty meat.

clue.text: Wild celebrants treat the town so? Small model was upsetting

definitions.text: Wild celebrants treat the town so?

blocks.note: the Mini is a small car model
what's eating you? means what is upsetting you

explanation.surface: Revellers go wild on the town while a small model was a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: Partygoers 'paint the town red'; miniate means to paint red with minium (red lead).
explanation.definitionFit: To miniate is to colour red, and revellers proverbially paint the town red.

clue.text: Coming before activity of lions on the prowl

definitions.text: activity of lions on the prowl

blocks.clueFragment: activity of lions on the prowl
blocks.note: second meaning: hunting other animals as prey

explanation.walkthrough: The same word reads as pre-dating (earlier than) and predating (hunting as a predator).
explanation.definitionFit: Predating means both existing earlier than something and, as a predator, hunting prey.

clue.text: Speciality of Agen once, long fed on contact sport?

indicators.note: fed on means taking something in as food, so a piece is held inside another

blocks.note: to pine is to long for

explanation.surface: Was rugby once the speciality of a French town?
explanation.walkthrough: Agen, in south-west France, is famed for prunes; pruine is an obsolete spelling of prune.
explanation.definitionFit: Agen's prunes are a celebrated local product, and pruine is an old spelling of prune.

clue.text: Chemist's pot, quite filled with due liquid

indicators.note: liquid means flowing, so the letters flow into a new order
filled with says one piece is put inside the other

blocks.note: all can mean quite, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A chemist's pot is filled right up with the liquid it needs.
explanation.walkthrough: An aludel is a pear-shaped pot used in old sublimation apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: An aludel is a pot used by alchemists and chemists in sublimation.

clue.text: Part of sleeping quarters army regulation brought back for strict disciplinarian

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so the letters run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a dorm is one part of the sleeping accommodation
AR is the abbreviation for Army Regulation

explanation.surface: An army regulation about sleeping quarters is reinstated for a martinet.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramrod is a rigidly strict person, after the stiff rod used to load a musket.

clue.text: Shot worth little, moving first to last of course

indicators.note: moving the opening letter to the end rotates the word by one place

explanation.surface: A cheap shot that drifts first to last on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: In target shooting or archery the outer ring scores least, so a shot there is an outer.
explanation.definitionFit: An outer is a shot striking the outermost ring of a target, scoring the fewest points.

clue.text: After breather I put on simple wraparound

blocks.note: a lung is the organ you breathe with

explanation.surface: After a rest, I put on a simple wrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breather' suggests a pause, but here it is the organ that breathes. 'After' and 'put on' set I after LUNG. A lungi is a cloth wrapped round the waist in South Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A lungi is a length of cloth worn wrapped round the hips, a simple garment.

clue.text: Profits, something to argue about

definitions.note: plural noun; issue in this sense is a mass noun for produce or profits

blocks.note: first meaning: proceeds or produce, as from land
second meaning: a point in dispute

explanation.walkthrough: The legal sense of issue is the yield or profits of an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means the produce or proceeds of land and also a matter under dispute.

clue.text: Some aspiring manager, one employed by Hoover?

indicators.note: some means a portion, so only part of the wording is used

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A would-be manager is taken on by a vacuum-cleaner firm?
explanation.walkthrough: Hoover suggests the vacuum cleaner, but it is J. Edgar Hoover, long head of the FBI.
explanation.definitionFit: G-man is US slang for an FBI agent, and J. Edgar Hoover ran the FBI.

clue.text: I scour in jumble for bric-à-brac

indicators.note: a jumble is a disordered mixture, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: I search a jumble sale for knick-knacks.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumble sale is a British charity sale of second-hand goods, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Curios are small curious ornaments, the kind of collectable odds and ends called bric-a-brac.

clue.text: Mendicant old friar, termly struggling, I let in

indicators.note: struggling suggests writhing about, so the letters are thrown out of order
let in means admitted, so one piece goes inside the other

explanation.surface: A begging friar, struggling each term, says he let me in.
explanation.walkthrough: A limiter (old spelling lymiter) was a friar licensed to beg within fixed limits.
explanation.definitionFit: A lymiter was a medieval friar allowed to beg within a set district, so a mendicant one.

clue.text: Flower cut for altar canopy

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the final letter is removed

explanation.surface: Cut flowers are arranged for the altar.
explanation.walkthrough: Dais is used here in its older sense of a canopy over a seat of honour or altar.
explanation.definitionFit: Dais once meant a canopy over a throne or altar, before it came to mean the raised platform.

clue.text: Smell alongside eastern fan you'll find in passing

blocks.note: a vane is a blade of a fan

explanation.surface: An oriental fan gives off a fragrance that wafts by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' suggests an admirer or a hand fan; here it is a blade of a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: Evanescent means quickly fading away, so fleeting or passing.

clue.text: Dollar is not exorbitant rate (starters only) … for customers here?

indicators.note: starters are the opening items, so only the initial letter of each word is used

blocks.note: opening letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A restaurant whose prices in dollars are not steep, for its customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' doubles as the first course of a meal, apt for an eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: A diner is a small inexpensive American restaurant, a place where customers come to eat.

clue.text: Exercise for chanteuse from France, say, unaccompanied round

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece encloses the others

blocks.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: A French singer's exercise, sung alone as a round.
explanation.walkthrough: A round is also a kind of song, which disguises the container signal. F is the international vehicle code for France.
explanation.definitionFit: Solfège is a singing exercise using sol-fa syllables, as practised by a singer.
